I have been working this land for fifty years. I know this soil, I know the seasons in Quzhou, and I know what I can manage with just my wife and me. We do wheat first, then maize on the same ground — same as always, same as my father did.

**Wheat (October planting):** I will put wheat on all 14 mu. I always use the improved semi-winter variety from the county seed station — not the old traditional seed, that gives too little. I have learned to apply base fertilizer before sowing and top-dress at jointing. I use about 16 jin of urea equivalent per mu over the season. My well is reliable, so I will water three times: once at sowing to get germination, once at jointing, once at heading. That is usually enough. Two sprays — one herbicide in winter, one for rust and aphids in spring. I do rotary tillage before sowing, easier on my back than the plough.

**Maize (June planting, right after wheat harvest):** All 14 mu again. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — I have used it for over twenty years, good yield, I trust it. Summer has rain here, so I only irrigate twice if it is dry: at tasseling and at grain fill. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide after emergence, one for corn borer. I seed directly without deep tillage to save time between the wheat harvest and maize planting. The ground stays moist and I cannot afford to lose planting days.

Two of us cannot do fancy things. I keep it simple and reliable.
